proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a sharp two-row sharing versus ground-untying frontier for count-score queries, with source-preserving finite witnesses and a conditional validation response-set result. Both math and decision panels passed after an editorial citation repair, but the cold novelty review graded the delivered result incremental below the fixed field floor. A concrete repeated-N3 validation design and its feasible response geometry remain open; the reviewer found that extension outside bounded in-scope salvage.
tldr: A known randomized traffic policy exposes two source-unsupported full typed parent-multiset contexts of one shared binary brake mechanism across \(m\) cars. For every source law compatible with the recursive binary full-input \(\rho\)-Markovian RSCM class, a source-local canonicalization yields finite common-noise witnesses and makes the shared row set exactly \([0,1]^2\), while a deliberately untied ordinary ground-SCM comparator has the cube \([0,1]^{m\times2}\). Every bounded count-score frontier factors through the policy count law \(w\), has a sharp four-corner endpoint criterion, and has sharp worst normalized distortion \(1-a_\pi^\star\). A three-car correlated policy has exact shared range \([0,9/16]\) for exactly one brake, scalar-diagonal image \([0,4/9]\), and untied range \([0,1]\). Conditional on an exact realizable response set supplied as validation information, a supporting theorem gives its exact score image and nine support-stratum endpoint tests. Deriving that response set and its geometry from specified validation skeletons, interventions, and laws remains open.
gap: Relational SCM theory establishes qualitative nonidentification at unseen traffic contexts, while finite response-function, polynomial-program, symbolic-bound, and credal-network methods provide general representations and optimizers. None of these sources characterizes the analytic distortion from deleting two shared relational response rows under a correlated known context policy.
fill: The project proves source-preserving two-way finite witnesses, derives the shared square and untied cube rather than positing them, gives both sharp intervals and their endpoint-preservation frontier, supplies a strict rational two-row example, quantifies the sharp worst score distortion, and bounds sensitivity to nonanonymous utilities.
